slides.heading: break Statements
slides.body: break Statements is part of Indefinite Iteration. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: break Statements
slides.body: The break statement stops a loop immediately. It is useful when the loop has found what it needs.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: break is like pressing an emergency stop button on a machine.

annotations.note: This line starts a loop that continues while the condition remains true.
This line displays a value or message on the screen.
This line stops the loop immediately.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Every while loop needs a condition that can eventually become False, unless you intentionally stop it with break.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Write a loop that prints Stop once, then breaks.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Use break so a while True loop prints Found only once.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
